testName: Class B Knowledge Test #1 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: When turning quickly to avoid an object in the road, what should you do?

options.text: Apply your brakes while you steer.
Turn more than needed to give extra clearance.
Turn just enough to miss the object. Do not turn more than necessary.
Steer and speed up at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn just enough to miss the object. Do not turn more than necessary.
questions.explanation: Turn only as much as needed to miss the object. Do not brake while turning.

questions.question: How should you brake when your vehicle has ABS?

options.text: Pump the brake pedal.
Brake normally.
Brake harder than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake normally.
questions.explanation: With ABS, brake the same way you would with any other braking system. Do not change how you brake.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a vehicle inspection report?

options.text: It tells the motor carrier about problems that need to be fixed.
It ensures the vehicle is inspected regularly.
It holds drivers responsible for checking their vehicles.
It provides a plan for the next five trips.

questions.correctAnswerText: It tells the motor carrier about problems that need to be fixed.
questions.explanation: A vehicle inspection report informs the motor carrier about issues that could affect safe operation. Drivers should complete one after each day of driving and note any problems that could affect safety or cause breakdowns.

questions.question: What is Gross Vehicle Weight (GVW)?

options.text: The total weight of the vehicle plus its cargo.
The total weight of the vehicle without cargo.
The weight of the cargo only.
The maximum weight allowed to be transported.

questions.correctAnswerText: The total weight of the vehicle plus its cargo.
questions.explanation: Gross Vehicle Weight (GVW) is the combined weight of a vehicle and all its cargo.

questions.question: If you are convicted of a traffic violation in your personal car, what must you do?

options.text: Tell your employer.
Your CDL will not be affected.
Law enforcement will tell your employer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell your employer.
questions.explanation: You must notify your employer within 30 days of any traffic conviction, no matter what vehicle you were driving. Parking violations do not count.

questions.question: If you are disqualified from driving, what must you do?

options.text: The state will notify your employer.
Tell your employer within two business days.
Tell your employer within one month.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell your employer within two business days.
questions.explanation: You must notify your employer within two business days if your license is suspended, revoked, canceled, or if you are disqualified from driving.

questions.question: What should you do with a trailer's load?

options.text: Overload it to work more efficiently.
Do not overload it because it is dangerous.
Do not overload it because drivers are only paid for certain weights.
Put all weight directly behind the cab.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not overload it because it is dangerous.
questions.explanation: Overloading a vehicle is dangerous. It can damage the vehicle and make it harder for you to control.

questions.question: When you start a vehicle, what should the coolant temperature do?

options.text: Decrease.
Rise slowly.
Stay the same.

questions.correctAnswerText: Rise slowly.
questions.explanation: After starting, the coolant temperature should gradually increase toward the normal operating range.

questions.question: What does an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) do?

options.text: Let the rear wheels lock up.
Let all wheels lock up.
Help stop the wheels from locking up.
Alert other drivers when you brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help stop the wheels from locking up.
questions.explanation: ABS prevents the wheels from locking up when you brake hard on a slippery road.

questions.question: What should you do when going down a steep hill?

options.text: Use the air brakes.
Shift to a lower gear, then use brakes to add to the engine's braking power.
Keep downshifting instead of using brakes.
Drive on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to a lower gear, then use brakes to add to the engine's braking power.
questions.explanation: Use the engine's braking power as your main way to control speed on a downhill grade. Shift to a lower gear before the hill and use brakes only for extra stopping power if needed.

questions.question: How should you adjust your mirrors before driving?

options.text: Your vehicle should not be visible in any mirror.
You should be able to see part of your vehicle in the mirrors.
More than half of each mirror should show your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should be able to see part of your vehicle in the mirrors.
questions.explanation: When mirrors are properly adjusted, you should see part of your vehicle in each one. Seeing your vehicle helps you judge where other objects are on the road.

questions.question: What must you do before transporting an over-length load?

options.text: Get special permits from the Department of Transportation.
Alert the fire departments along your route.
Pay tolls in advance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get special permits from the Department of Transportation.
questions.explanation: Loads that are over-length, over-width, or overweight require special permits from the Department of Transportation.

questions.question: What happens if brakes overheat going down a hill?

options.text: They become sticky.
They stop working.
They squeak.

questions.correctAnswerText: They stop working.
questions.explanation: Using brakes too much can cause them to overheat and lose effectiveness. This is called brake fade.

questions.question: What is axle weight?

options.text: The weight that one axle puts on the ground.
The weight of the axle itself.
The maximum weight an axle can hold.

questions.correctAnswerText: The weight that one axle puts on the ground.
questions.explanation: Axle weight is the weight transmitted to the ground by one axle or one set of axles.

questions.question: If the previous driver left a vehicle inspection report, what should you do?

options.text: Skip your own pre-trip inspection and trust the report.
Take the vehicle to a mechanic.
Read the report.
Talk to the previous driver about it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Read the report.
questions.explanation: The first step of a vehicle inspection is to read any report left by the previous driver.

questions.question: What should you do before driving a vehicle with a dual brake system?

options.text: Let the engine warm up so fuel reaches it properly.
Wait for air pressure to build up in both brake systems.
Start driving right after the engine starts.
Pump the brake pedal about 20 times, then start driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for air pressure to build up in both brake systems.
questions.explanation: Before driving a vehicle with dual air brakes, let the compressor build air pressure to at least 100 psi in both systems.

questions.question: What happens if you drive a commercial vehicle with any detectable alcohol, even below the legal limit?

options.text: You will be ordered out of service for 2 hours.
You will be ordered out of service for 10 hours.
You will be ordered out of service for 24 hours.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will be ordered out of service for 24 hours.
questions.explanation: If you have any detectable amount of alcohol in your system while driving a commercial vehicle, even if your blood alcohol level is below 0.04 percent, you will be ordered out of service for 24 hours. Never drive while under the influence of alcohol.

questions.question: How many tie-downs are needed at minimum to secure a 10-foot piece of cargo?

options.text: One
Two
Three

questions.correctAnswerText: Two
questions.explanation: On flatbed trailers, you need at least one tie-down for every 10 feet of cargo. However, you must use at least two tie-downs no matter the cargo size.

questions.question: What is the main factor that determines your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?

options.text: How much alcohol you drink.
How often you drink.
The temperature of the drink.

questions.correctAnswerText: How much alcohol you drink.
questions.explanation: Your BAC depends mainly on how much alcohol you consume, how fast you drink it, and your body weight.

questions.question: What will you be asked to do during the vehicle inspection test?

options.text: Explain what you inspect and why.
Replace an electrical fuse.
Unload the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Explain what you inspect and why.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, you must do a complete inspection and explain to the examiner what you are checking and why.

questions.question: When should you do an after-trip inspection?

options.text: Once a week.
Once a month.
After every trip.

questions.correctAnswerText: After every trip.
questions.explanation: You must inspect your vehicle after every trip or at the end of your work day. Fill out a vehicle inspection report if required.

questions.question: When changing lanes, when should you use your turn signal?

options.text: Always.
Only when other traffic is present.
Only between dusk and dawn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always.
questions.explanation: You must always use your turn signal before turning or changing lanes.

questions.question: What happens if you start a left turn before reaching the center of the intersection?

options.text: You will likely complete the turn safely.
You may hit other vehicles with the left side of your vehicle.
Other drivers will move their vehicles to let you turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may hit other vehicles with the left side of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Wait until you reach the center of the intersection before turning left. If you turn too early, your vehicle's left side may swing out and hit another vehicle.

questions.question: Is it important to know what is happening behind your vehicle while driving?

options.text: No.
Yes.
It is distracting.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes.
questions.explanation: Always be aware of what is happening behind and beside your vehicle. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder as part of your normal scanning routine.

questions.question: What is tire load?

options.text: The maximum air pressure for a tire.
The maximum safe weight a tire can carry at a certain pressure.
The minimum safe weight a tire can carry.
The average weight of all tires on a vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum safe weight a tire can carry at a certain pressure.
questions.explanation: Tire load is the maximum safe weight that a tire can carry at a certain pressure. This number is printed on the side of the tire.

questions.question: If there are two left turn lanes at an intersection, which should you use?

options.text: The right lane.
It does not matter which lane you use.
The left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right lane.
questions.explanation: You may need to swing right to make a safe left turn. Always start your left turn in the rightmost left turn lane.

questions.question: When loading a trailer, what should you do with the weight?

options.text: Put as little weight as possible over the axles.
Put the right amount of weight over the axles.
Do not worry about how weight is spread out.
Put weight only over the axles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Put the right amount of weight over the axles.
questions.explanation: Cargo weight should be balanced evenly. Too much or too little weight on an axle can cause control problems and damage the axle.

questions.question: Which item should you NOT check in the engine compartment?

options.text: Engine oil level.
Coolant level in the radiator.
Windshield washer fluid level.
Fuel level.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fuel level.
questions.explanation: Check your oil level, coolant level and hose condition, power steering fluid level, windshield washer fluid, battery connections and fluid level, transmission fluid level, and belt condition. Also check for leaks and damaged wiring. Do not check fuel level in the engine compartment.

questions.question: What is sleep debt?

options.text: When you do not get enough sleep.
When you want to take a nap.
Too much sleep.
The time it takes to be ready to drive after sleeping.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you do not get enough sleep.
questions.explanation: Sleep debt happens when you do not sleep enough. You can only pay back this debt by sleeping more.

questions.question: Is a ramp's posted speed limit safe for all vehicles?

options.text: Yes, it is safe for all vehicles.
It is safe for some vehicles, but may be too fast for large trucks.
No, speed limits on ramps are just suggestions.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is safe for some vehicles, but may be too fast for large trucks.
questions.explanation: Posted speed limits on ramps are safe for cars but may be too fast for large or heavy trucks. Large truck drivers should drive slower than the posted speed limit.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system, how long should it take for air pressure to build from 85 to 100 psi?

options.text: Two minutes.
15 seconds.
10 minutes.
45 seconds.

questions.correctAnswerText: 45 seconds.
questions.explanation: When inspecting a vehicle with a dual air brake system, air pressure should build from 85 to 100 psi in both the primary and secondary systems in about 45 seconds.

questions.question: How should you hold the steering wheel?

options.text: Held with both hands.
Held with one hand to keep the other hand free.
Held with one hand at a time, alternating between hands.

questions.correctAnswerText: Held with both hands.
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel firmly with both hands, placed on opposite sides of the wheel.

questions.question: Why are roads especially slippery when it first begins to rain?

options.text: Water is always very slippery.
The fresh rain mixes with oil on the roadway.
The water has nowhere to go.

questions.correctAnswerText: The fresh rain mixes with oil on the roadway.
questions.explanation: Roads are especially slippery when it first rains. The water mixes with oil drippings on the road that have not yet been washed away, creating a slippery surface.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a distracted person that motorists should worry about?

options.text: A driver talking to another person in a vehicle
Children on the side of the road
Construction workers on the side of the road
A person sitting on a bench waiting for a bus

questions.correctAnswerText: A person sitting on a bench waiting for a bus
questions.explanation: Drivers talking to passengers may not pay full attention to the road. Children may dart into the road without looking. Drive carefully near road workers to keep them safe. A person sitting on a bench waiting for a bus is not a concern.

questions.question: What is the only way to sober up after drinking alcohol?

options.text: Take a cold shower.
Exercise.
Wait.
Drink coffee.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait.
questions.explanation: Your liver removes alcohol from your body at a fixed rate. Nothing can speed this up—not coffee, showers, or exercise. The only way to sober up is to wait.

questions.question: How should you conduct pre-trip inspections?

options.text: Differently each time, emphasizing different items.
The same way each time so you are less likely to forget something.
Once in a while.
By someone other than the driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same way each time so you are less likely to forget something.
questions.explanation: Do pre-trip inspections the same way every time. This helps you remember to check everything important.

questions.question: What is another name for front-end header boards?

options.text: Headache racks
Cargo stoppers
Head braces
Bonkers

questions.correctAnswerText: Headache racks
questions.explanation: Front-end header boards are also called "headache racks." They protect the driver from cargo that might move during a crash or emergency stop.

questions.question: What color are the malfunction lamps on vehicles with Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS)?

options.text: Green
Blue
Yellow

questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow
questions.explanation: Vehicles with ABS have yellow malfunction lamps. They turn on to alert you when the braking system is not working. Know where your malfunction lamp is before you drive.

questions.question: If a vehicle has an inspection report with it, what should you do?

options.text: Inspect the vehicle first, then compare your notes with the report.
Look at the report first when completing your inspection.
Skip your pre-trip inspection and only use the report.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look at the report first when completing your inspection.
questions.explanation: When you start a vehicle inspection, first review any inspection report left by the previous driver.

questions.question: During a static leakage test, what is the maximum safe air leak rate for a double combination vehicle?

options.text: 3 psi in one minute.
6 psi in one minute.
8 psi in one minute.

questions.correctAnswerText: 3 psi in one minute.
questions.explanation: For a double combination vehicle with air brakes, the air leak rate should not exceed 3 psi in one minute. If air leaks faster than this, do not drive the vehicle—it needs repairs.

questions.question: When carrying a sealed load, a driver should:

options.text: Open the load to check if it is safe.
Make sure the weight does not exceed the legal limit.
Check inside the container before driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the weight does not exceed the legal limit.
questions.explanation: You cannot open a sealed load to inspect it. However, you must still make sure the weight does not exceed the legal limit.

questions.question: Do not decide when to shift gears based on:

options.text: Your engine speed (rpm).
Your speed on the road (mph).
What other vehicles next to you are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: What other vehicles next to you are doing.
questions.explanation: Shift gears based on your engine's rpm range or your speedometer reading. Do not shift based on what other drivers around you are doing.

questions.question: How can you avoid getting drowsy while driving?

options.text: Get about three hours of sleep before you drive.
Plan your trip ahead of time and include rest stops.
Do not exercise regularly.
Drive at night instead of during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Plan your trip ahead of time and include rest stops.
questions.explanation: To avoid fatigue while driving, get seven to eight hours of sleep before you drive. Drive during the hours when you are normally awake. Plan to take breaks during your trip. Exercise regularly.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a sign of damaged brakes?

options.text: Cracked drums
Brake shoes with oil or grease on them
Brake shoes that are very thin
Brake pads that are clean and dry

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake pads that are clean and dry
questions.explanation: Signs of brake problems include cracked drums, brake shoes or pads with oil, grease, or brake fluid on them, and shoes that are worn too thin. Clean, dry pads are a good sign.

questions.question: Bent lock rings:

options.text: Are acceptable.
Are safe in dry weather.
Are unsafe.
Can make tires last longer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are unsafe.
questions.explanation: Bent, cracked, or mismatched lock rings are unsafe and must not be used.

questions.question: To be more visible to other vehicles at dawn or dusk, you should:

options.text: Turn on your four-way flashers.
Honk your horn.
Turn on your headlights.
Turn on your windshield wipers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your headlights.
questions.explanation: At dawn, dusk, and in snow or rain, turn on your headlights. This makes it easier for other drivers to see your vehicle.

questions.question: When checking the exhaust system, it should be:

options.text: Loose.
Leaking.
Securely fastened.
Cracked.

questions.correctAnswerText: Securely fastened.
questions.explanation: Check that all exhaust system parts are secure. Do not drive if any parts are loose, broken, or missing.

questions.question: To help other drivers see your vehicle, your lights should be:

options.text: Clean.
Off during daytime driving.
Covered with grease.
Used only when it rains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Clean.
questions.explanation: Keep your lights clean so they shine brightly. This helps other drivers see you at night.

questions.question: Roads are especially slippery when rain first starts because:

options.text: Water mixes with oil and grease already on the road.
Tires cannot grip wet roads.
Water has not yet washed away the dirt and grease.

questions.correctAnswerText: Water mixes with oil and grease already on the road.
questions.explanation: When rain first starts, it mixes with oil and grease on the road surface to form a slippery film.

questions.question: During the pre-trip inspection, when you start the vehicle, the coolant temperature should:

options.text: Go down.
Go up slowly.
Stay the same.
Go up quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go up slowly.
questions.explanation: After starting your vehicle, watch the gauges. The coolant temperature should rise gradually to its normal operating level.
